events.note: Authored for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up) from the contract claims and handoffs E1, E2 and E3 cited in the expectation, before any scanner was consulted; carrier existence is provider-documented, the context policy is project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up), on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases and baselines authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2). No dissent was raised by the maintainer; the strongest counter-argument is recorded in the dissent field. Question: The encoded credential after Basic in an Authorization header carrying a Zendesk API token string is a credential whatever its shape, covered whole? Options: flag only the token-only forms already decided (the encoded run has no decoded token-only span); require a documented token format (none is stated); or flag the whole encoded run as the Batch 2 Basic-envelope Cases do. Decision: flag the whole encoded run after Basic, no subtype inference and no era exception. Reason: Zendesk documents the carrier and the encoding step but not a token format, so the expectation rests on project policy and is not a provider rule; this follows the Basic-envelope decisions already recorded for other families. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's instruction.
events.dissent: The encoded run also covers the email address, whose confidentiality Zendesk does not state, so a whole-run span over-covers; a position rule can flag a non-Zendesk Basic credential; the family is being retired, so the protected value may stop working; leaving the case a draft would claim nothing.
events.reversingEvidence: A Zendesk statement of the token format or of the email address's confidentiality that contradicts this outcome, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
